findings.title: oidc_callback() fetches token_endpoint/jwks_uri from the discovery document with only a scheme check
findings.evidence: if not token_endpoint.startswith(("https://", "http://")) or not jwks_uri.startswith(("https://", "http://")):
findings.fix: call _oidc_helpers.assert_safe_public_https_url() on token_endpoint and jwks_uri (and on authorization_endpoint at mfa.py:1777) before either fetch, mapping ValueError to the existing invalid_discovery_document redirect — the issuer_url the document came from already passes that same guard via schemas/auth.py:_validate_issuer_url, so the endpoints it declares should not escape it
findings.behavior_change_note: an IdP whose discovery document declares an http:// or private-address token_endpoint/jwks_uri would stop working: its users' logins would bounce to /?oidc_error=invalid_discovery_document instead of completing.

findings.title: forgot_password() records the per-email rate event only for real local users, so its 429 is an account-existence oracle
findings.evidence: db.add(AuthRateLimitEvent(username=identifier, event_type=EventType.PASSWORD_RESET_SEND))  # staged only inside `if user and user.is_active and user.auth_source not in ("ldap", "oidc")` — the per-IP cap is 10, so 4 requests for one address return 429 for a local account and the generic 200 for an unknown one
findings.fix: stage the PASSWORD_RESET_SEND event for the normalised identifier unconditionally, alongside the PASSWORD_RESET_IP event, instead of inside the user-exists branch
findings.behavior_change_note: a visitor who submits the same unknown or SSO-only email 3 times in 15 minutes now gets 429 'Too many password reset requests' on the 4th attempt, where today every attempt returns the generic success message.

findings.title: checkAuthStatus() adopts any ?token= from the URL on every route, overwriting a live session and persisting it once validated
findings.evidence: setAuthToken(urlToken, 'session'); // session-only until server confirms it's valid  … if (urlToken && token === urlToken) { setAuthToken(urlToken, 'persistent'); }
findings.fix: only adopt the URL token when no token is already stored, and require an explicit kiosk marker (e.g. a dedicated /kiosk route or a second query flag) before writing it — the L-4 comment only defers persistence past validation, it does not stop an attacker-supplied token being adopted in the first place
findings.behavior_change_note: SpoolBuddy kiosk links that today authenticate by appending ?token= to any page URL would stop working until they are re-issued against the kiosk entry point, and a ?token= link would no longer replace an already-signed-in session.

findings.title: oidc_callback() logs the attacker-controlled `error` query parameter with %s
findings.evidence: logger.warning("OIDC callback received error: %s", error)  # `error: str | None = Query(default=None, max_length=256)` on a route in PUBLIC_API_ROUTES
findings.fix: log it as %r, matching the convention the rest of this module already uses for untrusted claim values (e.g. "…for sub=%r"), so newlines and control characters are escaped rather than forging log lines
